attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-05-15
Provider: Dr. Priya Patel, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Brought to the emergency department after a motorcycle accident.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This 33-year-old male with prior September 2020 ED presentation for severe back pain and inability to move his legs returns following a motorcycle accident. He was thrown from the vehicle and landed on his back.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Anterior cord syndrome (diagnosed 2020-09-15)
- Intermittent mechanical low back pain
- Seasonal allergic rhinitis

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Arthroscopic knee surgery, age 28

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Ibuprofen 400 mg PRN back pain
- Loratadine 10 mg daily PRN allergies

ALLERGIES:
Penicillin (hives)

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father: Hypertension
- Mother: Hypothyroidism
- Brother: Healthy

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Former smoker (5 pack-years, quit 2 years ago). Alcohol: Social (2-3 drinks per week). Occupation: Construction foreman.

VITAL SIGNS:
Temperature is 36.9°C (98.4°F), blood pressure is 84/60 mm Hg, and pulse is 52/min.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On arrival, he is awake and alert but unable to move either leg.
Neurologic exam shows complete paralysis of both lower extremities with flaccid tone and absent deep tendon reflexes. Pain, temperature, vibration, and proprioception are absent below the nipples. Anal tone is absent, and there is no response to bulbocavernosus reflex testing. Upper extremity function is intact. Foley catheter insertion yields 1.1 liters of retained urine.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-09-15
Provider: Dr. Miguel Rodriguez, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
He complains of severe back pain and is unable to move his legs.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
He has intermittent mechanical low back pain and seasonal allergic rhinitis. He is brought to the ED after motor vehicle collision in which he sustained a direct blow to his back.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Intermittent mechanical low back pain
- Seasonal allergic rhinitis

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Arthroscopic knee surgery, age 28

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Ibuprofen 400 mg PRN back pain
- Loratadine 10 mg daily PRN allergies

ALLERGIES:
Penicillin (hives)

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father: Hypertension
- Mother: Hypothyroidism
- Brother: Healthy

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Former smoker (5 pack-years, quit 2 years ago). Alcohol: Social (2-3 drinks per week). Occupation: Construction foreman.

VITAL SIGNS:
On examination, his blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Neurological examination reveals flaccid paralysis of both lower extremities with absent deep tendon reflexes. He has a loss of pain and temperature sensation starting from the T10 dermatome and below, but intact proprioception and vibratory sensation.

IMAGING:
MRI of the spine shows an anterior wedge compression fracture of the T8 vertebral body with associated swelling and signal change in the anterior aspect of the spinal cord.
